subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The interval of an octave between two notes of the same letter name spans how many semitones?
questions.explain: An octave spans twelve semitones from one note to the next of the same name.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is a:
questions.explain: C up to G spans five letter names, making a perfect 5th.

questions.q: 'Composing to a brief' means:
options: Composing music to meet a given set of requirements or purpose
questions.explain: Composing to a brief means writing music that fulfils a specified purpose or set of instructions.

questions.q: Which term refers to the tone quality or 'colour' of a sound that lets you tell a flute from a violin?
questions.explain: Timbre, or sonority, is the characteristic tone colour that distinguishes one instrument or voice from another.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which chord progression?
questions.explain: A perfect cadence moves from chord V to chord I, sounding finished.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using a metronome when practising a performance?
options: It helps you keep a steady, accurate tempo
questions.explain: A metronome sounds a steady beat, helping a performer keep an accurate and consistent tempo.

questions.q: A minor triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A minor triad stacks a minor 3rd then a major 3rd, giving its darker sound.

questions.q: Which note value lasts the longest?
questions.explain: A semibreve lasts four beats in 4/4, longer than a minim, crotchet or quaver.

questions.q: What does the term 'tutti' instruct in an orchestral score?
questions.explain: Tutti means 'all', instructing the whole ensemble to play together.

questions.q: A triad in 'first inversion' has which note in the bass?
questions.explain: In first inversion the third of the chord is the lowest sounding note.

questions.q: Which cadence creates a surprise by moving from chord V to chord VI instead of I?
questions.explain: An interrupted cadence moves from V to VI, surprising the listener who expects a perfect cadence.

questions.q: A sharp sign in front of a note does what?
options: Raises the pitch by a semitone
Lowers the pitch by a semitone
questions.explain: A sharp raises a note's pitch by one semitone.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: In a pop song, the section that repeats with the same words and main 'hook' is the:
questions.explain: The chorus repeats with the same lyrics and usually contains the song's main hook.

questions.q: 'Legato' means to play notes:
questions.explain: Legato means smooth and connected, with no gaps between notes.

questions.q: On a guitar, a 'capo' is used to:
options: Raise the pitch of all strings to play in a different key
questions.explain: A capo clamps across the fretboard to raise the pitch of every string, changing the key.

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

questions.q: Which Italian tempo term means 'fast and lively'?
questions.explain: Allegro means fast and lively, whereas adagio and largo are slow.

questions.q: What does a single dot placed after a note do to its value?
options: Adds half the note's value again
questions.explain: A dot after a note increases its length by half of its original value.

questions.q: Which time signature is an example of compound time?
questions.explain: 6/8 is compound time because each beat divides into three quavers (two dotted-crotchet beats).

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.

questions.q: What does a 'crescendo' instruct a performer to do?
questions.explain: A crescendo is a gradual increase in volume, opposite to a diminuendo.
